Computing epoch seconds via an explicit `datetime64[s]` cast is resolution independent.

Converting explicitly to `datetime64[s]` before casting to int64 makes the epoch-second result independent of the underlying resolution.

Dividing by 1e9 therefore produces seconds/1000. Forcing the column to `datetime64[ns]` before casting to int64 restores nanosecond epoch values on both old and new pandas.

With pandas 3.0 copy-on-write this chained set is a no-op and silently leaves `observed` all 1s, while pandas 2.3 mutated in place.
